title: Modularity of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons
summary: Starting after elliptic modularity, this roadmap makes residual comparisons effective. It develops sharp weight-two newspace estimates, the norm bound at a removed multiplicative prime, Kraus’s exact-conductor full-two-torsion realization, uniform rational-isogeny irreducibility consequences and Lemos’s restricted surjectivity theorem. Generic newforms, modularity, level lowering and elliptic-curve carriers remain with their existing owners.

# Modularity of elliptic curves over Q, Part II: effective residual comparisons

## Purpose and boundary

EllipticCurveModularity supplies modularity over Q and comparisons of compatible systems. This Part II addresses a different question: how large must a residual prime be before a congruence forces a stronger conclusion? Its first quantitative argument uses one multiplicative prime removed from a conductor. Its second uses an explicit threshold to replace an elliptic curve by a full-two-torsion curve of exactly the residual conductor. Uniform irreducibility consequences and the rational-cyclic-isogeny case of Serre uniformity form separate endpoints.

The common input is an actual normalized weight-two newform with trivial character. Its coefficients, coefficient field, Galois conjugates and residual representation are not arbitrary compatible data. The coefficient field must be the one generated by the coefficients of that form, its ring of integers must use the same inclusion into that field, and the prime above the residual prime must be the one in the congruence. Every norm and every coefficient embedding in the estimates refers to these objects.

No modularity theorem, generic newform, generic isogeny, generic Weil estimate or generic norm construction is rebuilt here. The new mathematical work is the sharp arithmetic estimate, its effective comparison applications, and the source-specific classification arguments. A theorem about a fixed curve outside finitely many residual primes is not a uniform numerical cutoff. Likewise, Lemos's conclusion for curves with a nontrivial rational cyclic isogeny is not the unrestricted uniformity conjecture.

## Conventions

Write g(N) for the complex dimension of the **trivial-character newspace**, at positive integer level N. At the pinned library, cuspFormsNew(N,2) is a subspace of cusp forms on Gamma1(N). Thus g(N) is the finrank of its intersection with cuspFormCharSpace(2,1), transported to Gamma0(N) by the existing trivial-character equivalence. Using the dimension of the entire Gamma1 newspace changes the estimate and the thresholds. Finite dimensionality and the comparison with the classical dimension are theorem inputs, not inferred from the total finrank function.

Write I(N)=[SL2(Z):Gamma0(N)]. Its Euler product is N times the product of 1+1/p over the distinct prime divisors p of N. This positive index is called mu in the Kraus application; here I avoids confusion with the Möbius function. The prime-power factors in the dimension expression use the separate Möbius correction. Factorization, primeFactors, totient, subgroup index, real square root, field norm and finite dimension use the existing library meanings.

An elliptic curve is the native Weierstrass curve over Q with its ellipticity hypothesis, not a new bundled curve type. End over Qbar equals Z is the non-CM condition in the Lemos endpoint. The conductor M and a nonzero minimal discriminant Δ are those of the same curve. The notation ord_q(Δ) means the nonnegative valuation exponent, not the prime power q raised to that exponent.

Keep three level quantities distinct. M is the original conductor. M0 is obtained by deleting q once when q divides M exactly once and the residual prime ell divides ord_q(Δ). N is the prime-to-ell Artin conductor of the residual representation. The identity M0=N requires a coefficient-prime and Serre-weight argument; it is not part of the definition of either level. The removed prime p in the norm argument is different from ell. The p in the Lemos endpoint is instead the residual prime; each theorem names its role.

All inequalities with fractions or square roots are inequalities of rational or real numbers. In particular N−6, N−9 and N−18 in the arithmetic estimates are not truncated subtraction in the natural numbers. Integer exponents and real exponents are distinguished when passing from 2[K:Q] to (M0+1)/6. The base sqrt(p)+1 is greater than one where exponent monotonicity is used.

## Dependency and source ownership

The analytic ModularForms roadmap supplies the full Gamma0 dimension formula and index/cusp/elliptic-point counts in Layer 10. Its Layer 4 supplies the primitive-form divisor decomposition, including multiplicity equal to the number of divisors of N/d. Layer 3 supplies the old/new and character-space conventions. Layer 8 supplies integral coefficients and the coefficient number field; Layer 8G supplies Galois stability and the orbit-degree comparison. These roles are not interchangeable: an old/new complement at one level does not by itself give the divisor multiplicities.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation supplies the qualified level-lowering and coefficient-prime cases. EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6 supplies unconditional modularity of the original curve. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4 supplies the local comparison with the special representation. Its R19.6 weight-two abelian realization, combined with DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.1/weil-estimate-for-abelian-varieties, supplies the bound for all conjugates of a good Hecke coefficient. The latter existing node is reused directly. Analytic continuation of an L-function is not a substitute for this Weil bound.

The source-specific argument starts with Bennett–Siksek, §2, and Martin's prime-power dimension formula and sharp bound. The full Kraus proof, the Mazur–Kenku classification proof and the complete Lemos formal-immersion and finite-image certificates are required by the final three layers. Their endpoint contracts below preserve their hypotheses even where a granular proof is not yet supplied. No independent review or implementation is asserted by these specifications.

## Reading the declaration specifications

The namespace for new arithmetic declarations is TauCeti.EffectiveEllipticComparison. Each definition below has evaluation or characterization APIs and discriminating tests. Statements about native modular or elliptic objects are mathematical specifications, not replacement proposition fields. The accompanying suggested file omits the untypeable geometric endpoint rather than introducing a surrogate that assumes it.

## Layers

EC.0. Develop Martin’s exact prime-power correction table and its weight-two expression. Compare it to the existing trivial-nebentypus newspace using the upstream full dimension formula and old/new divisor multiplicities. Prove g(N)≤(N+1)/12 for every N>0, including equality exactly at 35 and primes congruent to 11 modulo 12. Separate each large-level estimate and finite certificate.

EC.1. For an irreducible elliptic residual representation at ell≥3 and a removed multiplicative prime p≠ell, prove ell≤(sqrt(p)+1)^((M0+1)/6). Keep the explicit deletion level, integral norm, nonvanishing, all embeddings, coefficient orbit size and local trace congruence as separate inputs. Do not identify the deletion level with the prime-to-ell residual conductor without a coefficient-prime theorem.

EC.2. Define F(N), G(N), H(N) from the actual Gamma0 index and trivial-character newspace dimension. Prove their evaluation APIs, boundary tests and maximum criterion. The square roots, factor 2 in the exponent and lcm(N,4) are fixed conventions.

EC.3. For E/Q with full rational two-torsion, ell≥5 prime, irreducible E[ell] of Serre weight two and prime-to-ell residual conductor N, prove that ell>H(N) produces F/Q of conductor exactly N with full rational two-torsion and the same residual representation. Follow Kraus, Théorème 4: finite coefficient recognition, rationality, elliptic realization and the two-torsion isogeny selection are distinct proof obligations. Prove the M0=N adapter in every application before substituting the deletion level.

EC.4. Prove the uniform Mazur–Kenku consequences: full rational two-torsion implies irreducibility at every prime ell≥7; a rational point of order two implies irreducibility at every prime ell≥11. Build the required rational cyclic isogeny classification argument and its finite exceptions here, importing existing torsion and isogeny constructions. Do not substitute R29.1’s fixed-curve finite-exception assertion, or add a reverse dependency from the modularity proof.

EC.5. Prove Lemos’s theorem: if End over Qbar of E/Q is Z and E admits a nontrivial cyclic Q-isogeny, then its mod-p Galois representation is surjective for every prime p>37. Separate subgroup elimination, the non-split Cartan local reduction argument, the formal-immersion theorem, integral-j classification and reproducible residual-image certificates. Do not export unrestricted Serre uniformity or replace finite certified calculations by a live database lookup.

## Sources

Greg Martin, Dimensions of the Spaces of Cusp Forms and Newforms on Γ0(N) and Γ1(N). https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0306128

Michael A. Bennett and Samir Siksek, A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums. https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v191-n2-p02-s.pdf

Pedro Lemos, Serre’s uniformity conjecture for elliptic curves with rational cyclic isogenies. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1702.01985

The roadmap is a partial plan; its declaration-level reader and packet state the precise proof and source obligations. Kraus’s original theorem and the Mazur–Kenku classification proofs remain required sources, not proved hypotheses.
